source_snapshot.procedure: Open the BMC Web LDAP page, set LDAP authentication and save; source asks to clear logs.
source_snapshot.criteria: LDAP authentication is set without errors.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL but only GETs LDAP config and shows truncated ipmitool help; it neither saves settings nor proves the source criterion and uses unsafe TLS/credential patterns.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION; staging LDAP, protected secrets/TLS, break-glass access, complete write/readback, optional owner-required functional login and baseline restoration.

historical_reviews.deepseek: Its staging-infrastructure warning is valid, but read-only JSON and CLI help cannot prove a successful configuration save.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Security, rollback and staging controls are accepted; functional login/role mapping is treated as an owner-confirmed extension because the literal criterion requires only setting without errors.
historical_reviews.history: Exact-code searches found no duplicate variant or completed record; other LDAP CRUD/certificate cases cannot supply this row's exact Web configuration contract.
historical_reviews.v3_1: An accepted LDAP configuration can still be operationally unusable, but the Review must distinguish the source's save/readback criterion from any additional bind/login/authorization checkpoint.

original_test_intent: With security approval, enter a complete owner-approved LDAP authentication configuration in the target BMC Web UI, save it without error, verify persistent readback and restore the prior authentication state without losing local recovery access.
original_method: Bind one BMC and snapshot its auth/LDAP baseline; validate a staging LDAP profile and TLS/CA material; through the supported Web/Redfish schema save only the approved fields, capture response and full redacted readback, optionally perform owner-required staging login/role validation as separately labelled evidence, then restore baseline and verify break-glass access.
manual_activity: The security owner supplies the staging directory, field values and secrets, approves the auth mutation and observes any optional login check; an operator maintains local/console recovery and confirms baseline restoration.
required_inputs: Exact SUT/BMC and supported LDAP Web/Redfish schema
Staging LDAP host/port, directory base and search attributes
TLS mode, hostname and CA chain
Save/readback acceptance and optional login/role scope
Restore/disable procedure and protected evidence storage
safety_requirements: Never target production LDAP for this test
Do not expose bind passwords, user secrets, tokens or private key material
Validate TLS/CA/hostname and avoid curl -k/password command lines
Verify break-glass access before enabling LDAP
Do not alter unrelated local accounts or role mappings
Stop on bind/TLS error, lockout, fallback loss or unexpected privilege
Do not clear audit or SEL logs and do not auto-retry
agent_execution_scope: Validate staging LDAP reachability and certificate facts without secret disclosure
Apply only approved fields after explicit confirmation
Capture complete save status and persistent redacted readback
Perform functional login/role checks only when separately owner-approved
Restore baseline and report facts without verdict
engineer_actions: Approve the full staging LDAP profile and security policy
Decide whether functional auth/role validation is in scope
Maintain break-glass recovery and approve restore
Resolve access failures and own PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: GET of AccountService/LDAP and `config -h ldap` are discovery/help only; they do not perform or verify the Web save required by the row, and their TLS/secret handling is unsafe.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: With security approval and break-glass verified, save one approved staging LDAP profile through the supported Web/Redfish path, capture complete status and redacted persistent readback, perform only separately approved functional auth checks, then restore the documented baseline.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: LDAP Web save and 30/30-minute estimates remain; functional login is not silently substituted for or added to the literal save-without-errors criterion.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a configuration ledger with baseline, approved redacted field matrix, certificate identity, save response, complete readback, optional separately labelled bind/login result and exact restoration proof.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds safe secret/TLS handling, actual write verification, recovery and restoration while preventing a read-only command from claiming the save criterion.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Successful save/readback proves configuration acceptance, not necessarily directory authentication or authorization; optional functional evidence must be clearly scoped.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: LDAP enablement can redirect all authentication or map excessive privilege even when settings save cleanly, so fallback access and staging isolation are mandatory.

project_override_considerations: If the Project defines `set LDAP authentication` as including test-user login and role mapping, that checkpoint must be explicitly approved with exact account/group expectations. Otherwise it remains supplementary evidence and does not expand the Master criterion.
expected_evidence: Redacted BMC and staging LDAP identity, baseline and approved field matrix
TLS/CA/hostname validation and protected secret-handling audit
Complete Web/Redfish save response and persistent redacted readback
Optional separately scoped test bind/login/role evidence when approved
Restored baseline/disable state and local/break-glass access verification
Audit/SEL security events and engineer-owned PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently require saving LDAP authentication without error. They do not explicitly require a login test; that distinction is handled as scope clarification rather than a conflicting target.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The configuration transaction is defined and becomes executable with normal security inputs: staging LDAP, field matrix, protected secrets, supported write path, fallback and restore.

review_improvement: Replaces read-only help output with the actual protected save/readback transaction, preserves the literal criterion and separately labels any functional authentication extension.
independent_technical_reasoning: A BMC may accept syntactically valid LDAP fields without successfully binding or assigning the intended role. Therefore save/readback and functional authentication are distinct checkpoints: the former is required by this row, while the latter must not be claimed or imposed unless the owner explicitly includes it.
